For the target video, <Picture 1> is referenced throughout.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Photorealistic live-action film footage of real actors in an ancient Chinese (Song-dynasty) period drama, with the look of a feature film. The one man in this shot is a short, portly man of fifty, filmed from behind him, in an ancient Chinese Song-dynasty rich landlord's dark gold silk cross-collared robe woven with small round medallions, with long wide sleeves and a black belt, and a small round black cap; the corner of the gate's small tiled roof and the evening sky shown in <Picture 1> are the set, keeping their layout. Initial composition: At the village entrance of Liuxi at dusk five days after the swarm night, up on the low earthen mound beside the gate; a warm orange-red evening sky, the sun just gone below the far hills: low-angle medium shot from behind and below him, framed from the waist up with clear sky above his cap: the portly man stands in the middle of the frame with his broad back square to the camera from the first frame, the back of his cap, the back of his thick neck and his rounded shoulders in dark gold silk toward the camera, his head facing straight away from the camera toward the village beyond; he is the only person in the frame; scornful and urgent: his shoulders hunched up stiff, his head jutting forward; above him, soft, the dark corner of the gate's small tiled roof at the upper left and the orange-red evening sky all around; their hands hold only what is described here. No second copy of anyone appears. The picture fixes the place and its light only, never the mood. The portly man leans forward over the edge of the mound toward the village and sweeps his flat right hand out from the left across to the right in one wide stroke, his wide sleeve swinging, then jabs the hand forward twice toward the village, his shoulders heaving, his broad back square to the camera the whole shot, the back of his cap toward the camera to the last frame, and the orange-red evening light stays unchanged. The camera holds a static shot. One continuous shot. The picture is clean, with no subtitles, captions or text anywhere on screen; a light evening breeze in the air, a clean natural film image. Natural, realistic human motion of a real actor: the weight of his heavy body moves as he leans and sweeps his arm, and the gold silk folds and swings over his back and sleeves.
